core_obligations: Reduce to a point of codimension zero (proof lines 1826-1832): let X' be the maximal open subspace which is a scheme and let x be a point of codimension zero; since points of codimension zero are dense it suffices to show that x lies in X'.

Produce an invariant affine open (proof lines 1832-1842): with R = U x_X U and its two projections, which are surjective finite etale, the fibre of the chart over x is finite, say eta_1, ..., eta_n, and each eta_i is a generic point of an irreducible component of U; since U is quasi-separated these finitely many points lie in an affine open W, which may be chosen invariant after enlarging it.

Conclude (proof lines 1842-1852): for an invariant affine open W the restriction R_W of the relation equals the preimages of W under the two projections and the two maps to W are again finite etale, so R_W is affine; hence the quotient W/R_W is a scheme by the groupoid proposition, and it is an open subspace of X containing x, so x lies in the maximal open subscheme X'.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the statement to showing that a codimension zero point lies in the maximal open subscheme.
Use finiteness of the fibre of the chart and quasi-separatedness of the cover to find an invariant affine open containing that fibre.
Apply the quotient result for a finite flat equivalence relation on an affine scheme.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if an algebraic space admits a finite etale surjective morphism from a quasi-separated scheme, then it contains a dense open subspace which is a scheme, containing every point of codimension zero (statement lines 1816-1824). The proof (proof lines 1826-1855) reduces to a codimension zero point, finds an invariant affine open containing the finite fibre of the chart by quasi-separatedness of the cover, and applies the quotient theorem for a finite flat equivalence relation on an affine scheme. H3: a three-step reduction with a genuine invariance step, written out in full.
